vopros: Should I pay for a tool that tracks whether ChatGPT and other AI assistants mention my business, or hire someone to get my business recommended by AI?

vyzhimka.tekst:
Short answer: **these aren't either/or — they solve different problems, and most businesses need at least a little of the second one before the first one is even useful.** Here's how to think about it.

## What each option actually does

**Tracking tools** (SE Ranking, Profound, Otterly.AI, Peec AI, Semrush AIO, etc.) work by sending industry-relevant questions to AI platforms like ChatGPT, Claude, and Google's AI Overviews multiple times per day, then collecting full AI responses and analyzing them for brand mentions, position in the response, and context of the mention. They're diagnostic — they measure whether your brand gets mentioned, how often, in what context, and alongside which competitors, rather than fixing anything.

**"Getting recommended" work** is a discipline usually called Generative Engine Optimization (GEO). It's the practice of making your business visible and citable to AI assistants so they mention or recommend you in their answers — search engines rank pages, while AI assistants synthesize answers from sources they trust and cite. GEO is about becoming one of those trusted sources. Practically, this means things like defining your business as a distinct entity with schema markup, creating extractable content like checklists and fact blocks, building authority through backlinks and consistent citations across directories, and optimizing for complete user questions instead of keywords.

## Why order matters

A tracker without an optimization effort just tells you a sad story on repeat. As one GEO guide puts it, tracking tells you where you're losing; fixing it is a separate job. Conversely, doing optimization work with zero measurement means you're guessing whether anything you did worked — you cannot improve what you do not measure.

## Practical recommendation based on your situation

**If you're a small/local business just starting out:** Skip paid tracking tools for now and put your first dollars into the fundamentals, because much of the "optimization" is really just doing your entity/citation hygiene well: fixing identity consistency — Organization schema and consistent NAP, Google Business Profile categories aligned with revenue services, LinkedIn pages matching site positioning, directory listings on Clutch and local chambers, and press/partner pages that mention your brand accurately. This is largely free or low-cost DIY work.

You can also manually spot-check yourself for free: manually prompt ChatGPT, Perplexity, and Google AI Mode with your top twenty buyer questions instead of paying for a tracker on day one.

**If you have a marketing budget and want efficiency:** A budget-friendly tracker like Otterly.AI is best for SMBs wanting a simple, budget-friendly way to track ChatGPT mentions and citations can be worth it — but treat it as a compass, not a fix. Look for one that pairs monitoring with action rather than just dumping data, since the best AI visibility platforms combine monitoring with actionable recommendations rather than leaving teams with raw data and no clear next steps.

**If you're going to "hire someone,"** make sure they're actually doing GEO work (content, schema, digital PR, review/citation building) — not just selling you a subscription to a monitoring dashboard rebranded as a service. A real program should include the full loop: analyzing which sources ChatGPT cites, identifying gaps where competitors appear but you don't, recommending what to fix or publish, tracking whether actions improved mention rate and share of voice, and attributing visibility improvements to content updates, technical fixes, PR placements, referral traffic, and conversions.

## Bottom line

- **Tiny budget / DIY-capable:** Do manual prompt checks + basic entity/citation cleanup yourself first. No paid tool needed yet.
- **Some budget, want visibility into competitors:** Get an affordable tracker (Otterly.AI, Peec AI-tier) to establish a baseline, then use the gaps it reveals to guide a few targeted fixes.
- **Real budget, this channel matters to your sales:** Hire someone to do the actual GEO work (schema, content, PR, review-building), and use a tracker as the report card for whether their work is paying off — not as a standalone purchase.

One caution: this space is young, vendor claims run hot, and stats like "X% visibility boost" circulating in marketing blogs should be treated skeptically since a GEO Score is a proprietary metric used to evaluate a page's readiness for AI-driven search, and it analyzes various factors to produce a quantifiable score — meaning every vendor's "score" is measuring something slightly different and there's no industry standard yet.
